neighbours.label: Naming a medical condition that co-occurs with or accompanies another (comorbidities, associated disorders, symptom clusters), vs medical-setting text that names no condition
fire: Adults with migraine are more likely to also suffer from depression and anxiety.
Celiac disease often occurs together with type 1 diabetes and thyroid disease.
Obesity is commonly linked with sleep apnea, high blood pressure, and gout.
Many children with autism also have epilepsy or chronic constipation.
Rheumatoid arthritis raises the risk of heart disease and osteoporosis.
Patients with cirrhosis frequently develop jaundice, swollen ankles, and confusion.
Down syndrome is often accompanied by heart defects and hearing loss.
People with allergies may also experience itchy eyes, sneezing, and sinusitis.
quiet: Adults with appointments should arrive ten minutes early and bring a photo ID.
The hospital opened a new wing with forty beds and a larger pharmacy.
Nurses record each patient's weight and height at every visit.
The doctor recommended walking for thirty minutes and drinking more water.
Many children at the clinic also bring a parent or a younger sibling.
Patients in the ward frequently ask for extra blankets, books, and tea.
The insurance plan covers two dental checkups and one eye exam a year.
Visitors with passes may also use the parking garage, cafe, and library.

predictions: Condition names in co-occurrence lists reach 0.25-0.6; clinic logistics text stays under 0.1.
